idea-plugin.name: Mapper Guard
idea-plugin.description:
Catches broken SQLAlchemy string references while you type — the ones that otherwise only fail when your app starts or a query runs.

  • relationship("Usre") — unknown mapped class
  • back_populates="adreses" — no such attribute on the target model
  • ForeignKey("usres.id") — unknown table or column
  • secondary="user_rolez" — unknown association table
  • session.query(User).filter_by(nmae=...) and Flask-SQLAlchemy's User.query.filter_by(...) — no such column

Also adds Ctrl+click navigation and completion inside all of those strings.

Built to stay quiet when your code is right: it only checks calls that resolve to SQLAlchemy, understands database column names that differ from attribute names, mixins, and duplicate model names across files. Tested on 9 open-source codebases (Superset, Airflow, MLflow, Redash, Indico, CTFd, Lemur, FlaskBB and Flask-AppBuilder — about 4,400 files) with zero false alarms; it found two real broken foreign keys in Lemur.

To turn it off: Settings → Editor → Inspections, search for “Broken SQLAlchemy string reference”. To silence one line: put # noinspection SqlaReference on the line above it.

Found a false alarm? Please open an issue with a short code snippet — every report becomes a test.

Not affiliated with or endorsed by the SQLAlchemy project.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.7 — If the plugin ever hits an error, the IDE can now send the report (only with your consent) to the developer, so it gets fixed quickly.

0.1.6 — Fixed a false alarm: models declared with __table__ = Table(...) no longer get warnings on their columns in filter_by() and back_populates (#1).

0.1.5 — First public release. Checks relationship("Class"), back_populates, secondary, ForeignKey("table.column") and filter_by(...) (including Flask-SQLAlchemy's Model.query), with Ctrl+click navigation and completion.
